claims.claim: Repo-To-Skill (arXiv:2609.02749) reports MLE-bench Any-Medal rising from 31.11% to 72.89% on the full 75-competition suite, a 41.78-point absolute and 134.3% relative gain.
The AREX-Skill repository snapshot contains 5,353 skills across 1,000 repository graphs, organized into 20 areas and 178 capability families.
The paper states that paper-derived and task-oriented skill graphs are not included in the 5,353 count, so the benchmarked skill sets are not the published library.
Section 4.3 states MLE-bench uses one descriptive skill graph for each of 75 competitions, built through task decomposition, source discovery, and bounded diagnostic trials.
The MLE-bench skill graphs were distilled from sources collected through web search, excluding only the original competition webpage and competition-specific content.

Appendix A.2.1 Table 5 gives the skill arm an Exploration phase capped at 24 GPU-hours per task plus a Running phase capped at 24 GPU-hours, while the no-skill baseline receives only the running budget.
The paper states the one-time construction budget is separate and is not counted in either run-time condition.
MLE-bench comprises 75 Kaggle competitions split 22 Low, 38 Medium, 15 High complexity, and its Low split is identical to the Lite subset.
MLE-bench's plagiarism check runs Dolos code fingerprinting against the top 50 public Kaggle notebooks per competition at a 60% similarity threshold and found zero flagged submissions.
The MLE-bench authors state that it is difficult to detect the reuse of high-level strategies, which is exactly what a distilled skill encodes.
MLE-bench's obfuscation experiment found 8.5 +/- 0.6% Any Medal on original descriptions versus 8.4 +/- 1.0% on obfuscated ones, but was run only on GPT-4o at an 8.5% medal rate.
MLE-bench's agent instructions forbid viewing others' solutions to the competition and threaten disqualification for plagiarism, but no rule governs pre-task preparation or internet access.
MLE-bench's grader awards bronze at a flat leaderboard position 100 for competitions with 250 to 999 teams, not at the top 10%.
Repo-To-Skill reports the High-complexity split rising from 13.33% to 62.22% Any Medal on 15 competitions over three runs, equivalent to roughly 6 of 45 competition-runs medalling versus 28 of 45.
Public first-place or top-placing solution write-ups with runnable code exist for at least 9 of the 15 High-complexity MLE-bench competitions and are first-page web search results.
The AREX-Skill library's 1,000 source repositories contain no repository whose owner or name includes kaggle, solution, 1st-place, winning, or competition, across all 178 family index files.
XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, scikit-learn and pandas have no skill directory in the AREX-Skill library, despite the tabular-modeling family's scope line naming gradient boosting.
The AREX-Skill repository publishes task-oriented skill graphs for FrontierCS, PaperBench and PassNet but not for MLE-bench.
Across the four benchmarks the relative gain is 134.3% for MLE-bench, 34.4% for PaperBench, 14.0% for PassNet and 9.2% for FrontierCS, and only FrontierCS carries a confidence interval.
SWE-Skills-Bench found 39 of 49 published agent skills produced zero pass-rate improvement, with a mean gain of 1.2% and token overhead up to 451%.

A controlled study found skill actual-use precision falls from 29.6% to 3.3% as skill pools grow from 5 to 100 entries, and that procedural anchoring accounts for 65.7% of skill benefit versus 4.5% for explicit knowledge injection.

Repo2Skill-Evo found every evaluated release transition invalidates part of the prior skill set across 105 transitions in 57 repositories, with frontier agents repairing them at only 29.9% to 69.7% macro F1.
MLE-bench's own budget ablations show GPT-4o rising from 8.7% to 11.8% Any Medal when the budget goes from 24 to 100 hours, and o1-preview rising from 16.9% pass@1 to 34.1% pass@8.
The best comparable score on OpenAI's official MLE-bench leaderboard is Famou-Agent 2.0 with Gemini-3-Pro-Preview at 64.44% Any Medal, dated 2026-02-23.
OpenAI paused new MLE-bench leaderboard submissions on 2026-04-24 while developing an improved process for ensuring submissions are fair and comparable.
Scale AI's search-contamination study measured an approximately 15% accuracy drop on the contaminated subset when the answer-bearing domain was blocked and the same questions re-run.
An independent audit of SWE-bench found 32.67% of successful patches had the solution present in the issue report or comments, dropping SWE-Agent plus GPT-4 on Verified from 22.4% to 10.0%.
Repo-To-Skill states library construction uses GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.6-sol at xhigh reasoning effort with an average allocation of about $40 per repository.
Repo-To-Skill reports MLE-bench results averaged over three repeated runs, whereas the original MLE-bench paper used 16 and 36 seeds for its headline AIDE rows.
MLE-bench full-75 Any Medal state of the art rose from 17.12% in October 2024 to 64.44% in February 2026 across successive published agents.

HASTE reports a 77.3% medal rate on MLE-bench Lite from a single-seed campaign, and a controlled ablation where tiered skill loading reaches 100% medal rate versus 62.5% for flat loading on 8 competitions.
Repo-To-Skill does not state the GPU model, vCPU count or RAM used for its MLE-bench graded runs, while MLE-bench's canonical envelope is 24 hours on 36 vCPUs, 440GB RAM and a single 24GB A10.
